title: QuantaPay Case Study Outline (Draft) — Dedicated capacity + strict latency SLOs
content:
DOC STATUS: Working outline for QuantaPay story. Not approved for public distribution. Claims/metrics placeholders MUST be validated (SE + telemetry) + approved by QuantaPay + Legal.

Primary angle (v0): Predictable low-latency LLM inference for payments workflows using Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) + rollout/fallback controls.
Secondary angle (optional): Operational simplicity + observability (Console) reduced firefighting during traffic spikes.

---

0) Working title options
- “QuantaPay hits strict p95 latency targets for real-time payment support with Redwood Dedicated”
- “Predictable LLM latency under load: QuantaPay moves from shared endpoints to reserved capacity”
- “From latency variance to SLA confidence: QuantaPay’s Dedicated deployment on Redwood”

Notes:
- Avoid “guaranteed” language unless we tie explicitly to Redwood SLA terms + QuantaPay’s own workload specifics.
- Consider using “consistent / predictable / reduced variance” phrasing.

---

1) TL;DR (web hero section)
QuantaPay uses Redwood Dedicated to run LLM inference for latency-sensitive fintech workflows. With reserved GPU capacity, workload-aware routing, and production observability, QuantaPay improved p95 latency and reduced tail spikes during peak traffic.

One-sentence metrics callout (placeholders):
- “Reduced p95 latency from [X] ms to [Y] ms at [Z] TPS.”
- “Cut timeout/error rate from [A]% to [B]% during peak windows.”
- “Maintained SLO: p95 < [SLO_TARGET] ms with burst handling up to [BURST_TPS].”

Metrics note: QuantaPay asked for caveats re: prompt length / model choice / region. Keep the metric statement scoped.

---

2) Customer snapshot (short)
Company: QuantaPay
Industry: Fintech / payments
Region(s): [TBD — likely NA + EU]
Stage: [TBD]
Team: Payments platform + applied AI
Use case(s):
- Real-time agent-assist / internal ops tools for payment investigation
- User-facing support flows that require low latency (confirm)
Why latency matters:
- Human-in-the-loop workflows (agent waiting)
- Checkout / payment operations have strict time budgets

---

3) Problem statement (what was broken / risky)
What they needed:
- Strict latency SLOs (especially p95/p99) during peak traffic
- Predictable throughput with minimal variance
- Ability to control rollout risk (avoid regressions during model/version changes)
- Clear visibility into token/cost + latency breakdowns for tuning

Constraints (from calls; keep high-level in public version):
- Data sensitivity (fintech); careful with logs/content retention wording
- Spiky traffic patterns (end-of-month / business-hour bursts)
- Procurement/security review requirements (don’t imply anything not contractually true)

Baseline situation (to confirm):
- They were using [baseline provider/self-hosted stack] and saw tail latency variance
- Hard to reserve predictable capacity without overprovisioning
- Inconsistent performance across model versions / infrastructure

---

4) Goals & success criteria (explicit + measurable)
Add a “What success looks like” box. Candidate bullets:
- Latency: p95 <= [SLO_TARGET_MS] ms for [SEQ_LEN/OUTPUT_LEN] with streaming [on/off]
- Throughput: sustain [SUSTAINED_TPS] with burst to [BURST_TPS]
- Reliability: error rate <= [ERR_TARGET]% (5xx + timeouts + 429s) within [MEASUREMENT_WINDOW]
- Operational: stable rollouts with automatic fallback when capacity constrained or errors spike

Definition notes:
- Must specify measurement window + percentiles + payload characteristics.
- Keep the numbers tied to a reproducible benchmark plan (traffic replay or synthetic harness).

---

5) Why Redwood (decision rationale)
What resonated (from demo/POC scoping):
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool for predictable throughput + data isolation
- Policy controls: rollouts / canaries / fallback policies
- Console: token-level + route/model dashboards (helped identify bottlenecks)
- Engineering support during POC: helped tune batching / rate limits / concurrency

Suggested “quote slot” (placeholder):
“Dedicated capacity plus the rollout controls gave us confidence we could meet our latency SLOs without overbuilding our own inference platform.” — [Name, Title], QuantaPay

---

6) Solution overview (what they implemented)
Public narrative should be concrete but not sensitive.

6.1 Deployment mode
- Redwood Dedicated
- Region: [TBD]
- Capacity: [# GPUs or ‘reserved capacity tier’] (might be too sensitive; use ranges or omit)

6.2 Request path (high-level)
- QuantaPay application -> Redwood API endpoint (Dedicated) -> model runtime
- Streaming: [on/off] (confirm; many low latency flows use streaming)
- Authentication: [TBD]
- Logging/retention: keep generic; align w/ security review guidance

6.3 Reliability / SLO controls
- Rate limiting / quotas configured for burst
- Fallback policy: [e.g., model variant or secondary region] (only include if they approve)
- Rollouts: canary for new model version with automatic rollback triggers

6.4 Performance tuning levers used (only if real)
- Continuous batching configuration
- KV/prefix caching where applicable
- Prompt/template changes? (be careful: may be sensitive / proprietary)

Callout box idea: “What we changed during the POC”
- Adjusted concurrency limits
- Updated client retry/backoff strategy
- Tuned timeouts for streaming endpoints
- Resolved one benchmark-window regression (see Risks/Notes)

---

7) Architecture section (case study diagram guidance)
We want a simple diagram suitable for web + PDF.

Draft diagram components:
- QuantaPay services (Payments Ops UI / Agent Assist) -> Redwood Dedicated endpoint
- Optional: QuantaPay observability (Datadog/CloudWatch) + Redwood Console
- Optional: “Rollout + fallback policy” box

Diagram notes:
- Do NOT include internal VPC CIDRs, account IDs, or anything that suggests network topology beyond “Dedicated capacity / isolated environment”.
- If they require: “Dedicated capacity in Redwood-managed environment” language.

---

8) Results / measurable outcomes (placeholders)
This section needs a single table + 2–3 narrative bullets.

8.1 Metrics table (draft)
Baseline vs Redwood Dedicated (POC or production — specify which)

- Latency (ms)
  - p50: [BASELINE_P50] -> [REDWOOD_P50]
  - p95: [BASELINE_P95] -> [REDWOOD_P95]
  - p99: [BASELINE_P99] -> [REDWOOD_P99]

- Throughput
  - Sustained: [BASELINE_TPS] -> [REDWOOD_TPS]
  - Burst: [BASELINE_BURST_TPS] -> [REDWOOD_BURST_TPS]

- Reliability
  - Timeout rate: [BASELINE_TIMEOUT]% -> [REDWOOD_TIMEOUT]%
  - 5xx rate: [BASELINE_5XX]% -> [REDWOOD_5XX]%
  - 429/rate-limit errors: [BASELINE_429]% -> [REDWOOD_429]% (if relevant)

- Operational
  - Time to detect/triage latency regressions: [BASELINE_TTR] -> [REDWOOD_TTR]
  - Incidents during POC window: [#] (optional)

Measurement details (must appear as footnote):
- Workload: [prompt length distribution], [output length], [streaming?]
- Window: [date range]
- Region + deployment mode
- Model: [model name/version] (confirm what they allow us to name publicly)

8.2 Narrative outcome bullets (choose 2–3)
- “Met strict p95 latency target of [SLO_TARGET] ms under peak load.”
- “Reduced tail-latency spikes during burst traffic by [X]%.”
- “Improved benchmark stability and repeatability with reserved capacity + consistent routing.”

Hard rule: no “up to” unless we define the exact conditions.

---

9) Proof points / screenshots to request (internal checklist)
- Redwood Console dashboard screenshot (latency percentiles by route/model) — confirm shareable
- Benchmark summary screenshot (traffic replay tool output) — likely internal-only
- Architecture diagram approval (QuantaPay brand/security)

Open question: QuantaPay may prefer we recreate charts in our own style rather than screenshot theirs.

---

10) Quotes (working list)
We need 1 exec/business quote + 1 engineering/ops quote.

Candidate speakers (TBD from AE):
- [Name], Head of Payments Platform
- [Name], Staff Engineer / Infra

Draft quote prompts:
- What triggered the change?
- What’s the cost of p95 latency misses?
- What did Dedicated let you stop worrying about?
- What surprised you (Console, rollout/fallback, support)?

Draft quote options (NOT APPROVED):
- “We needed p95 predictability more than we needed a bigger model. Redwood Dedicated gave us consistent performance we could plan around.”
- “The rollout and fallback controls let us move faster without risking production regressions.”

---

11) Security / compliance language (public-safe defaults)
Include a short “Security & governance” section, but keep it conservative.

Allowed phrasing candidate (needs Legal sign-off):
- “Dedicated capacity for workload isolation”
- “Audit logs and key management integrations available for regulated environments” (only if QuantaPay is actually using these features)

Avoid:
- Stating specific certifications unless current and verified for the timeframe.
- Any implication that QuantaPay data was used for training.

---

12) Risks / known issues (internal only; do not publish)
- Benchmark window saw a suspected p95 regression (SUP-2444). Need final root cause + confirm final numbers are post-mitigation.
- Customer redlined early draft language around “guarantees” and “always meets SLO” (see Soojin email thread).

---

13) Approvals + dependencies (who signs what)
QuantaPay (required):
- Approved company name/logo usage (or anonymized story decision)
- Approved quotes (verbatim) + titles
- Approved metrics + measurement footnote
- Approved architecture diagram detail level

Redwood (required):
- Legal: release form final (GC + commercial counsel)
- Security/claims review: Naomi Feldman (if required by program workflow)
- PMM: Soojin Lee final messaging pass

---

14) Next steps (week-by-week)
Week 1 (now):
- Confirm spokesperson + who approves (comms/legal)
- Lock measurement definitions + who provides baseline data

Week 2:
- Run final benchmark replay window (or pull production telemetry window)
- SE to validate p95/p99 methodology + confirm no regressions

Week 3:
- Draft v1 narrative + diagram v1
- Send to QuantaPay for redlines

Week 4:
- Incorporate redlines + finalize release form
- Prep web + PDF layout (Tessa team)

---

Appendix A: Question list for final validation call (internal)
- What is the exact SLO (number + definition + endpoint)?
- Streaming: did you measure TTFT separately from full response time?
- What request size distribution should we cite (p50/p95 tokens in/out)?
- Which region(s) and what times of day were measured?
- Are we allowed to name the model(s) used?
- Any constraints on describing fallback behavior?

Appendix B: Draft “Metrics footnote” template
“Metrics measured over [DATE_RANGE] using [TRAFFIC_REPLAY / PRODUCTION_TELEMETRY]. Latency reported as end-to-end client-observed response time for [WORKLOAD_DEFINITION], in region [REGION], using Redwood Dedicated. Results may vary based on prompt/output lengths, concurrency, and model configuration.”
